summary: Calorieshivam health and diet tracking app with camera-based food scanning, daily calorie logging, summaries/graphs/ratings, in-app helper chat, local rules-based nutrition estimation with optional weight input, a one-time body-goal onboarding, plus BMI + maintenance-calorie (TDEE) calculations from user profile data (height/weight/age/etc.) with a persistent dashboard area showing whether daily intake is above/below/at maintenance; additionally supports an optional personal health track-record/profile baseline where users can log lab/vitals values (e.g., CBC metrics like hemoglobin/platelets and blood pressure) to form a starting health profile; uses an aesthetic “S” logo across the app, and includes an Android (Play Store) build packaged from the existing web app via a WebView wrapper.
architectural_notes: Requires device camera integration (back camera) for food scanning.
AI/ML component needed for food recognition and nutrition estimation.
Conversational AI component for in-app chat support.
Data model should support daily logs and aggregated summaries for charts.
Branding assets update: replace existing logo with an aesthetic “S” across all UI surfaces (header/splash/empty states).
UX decision: place Scan action on main dashboard; tapping it opens camera immediately (no intermediate start screen).
Nutrition estimation must be fully local (no external AI/LLM calls), using a built-in Indian+global foods dataset and a 'similar food' fallback.
Add a one-time onboarding/profile setup for body goals capturing goal type, current weight, target weight, and weekly goal speed, stored per user.
Voice input: integrate on-device speech-to-text for meal description specifically within the food scanning flow; user can edit transcribed text before saving.
Weekly summary/score should be generated automatically from the user’s last-7-days logged entries using local rules/heuristics (no external AI/LLM calls), aligned with the user’s selected body goal.
known_issues: Camera/food scanning flow not currently visible or accessible in the deployed draft UI (only manual add-entry is apparent).

existing_features.title: Implement Internet Identity–based user flow so each signed-in user can create and view their own diet entries (no shared data across principals).
Create a Daily Dashboard page that shows: today’s total calories, a list of today’s logged foods, and an end-of-day (and selectable date range) total calorie summary.

Add interactive graphs and rating-style visualizations for engagement, including: calories over time (daily), macro distribution (today or selected day), and a simple daily “nutrition balance” rating derived from logged macros.
Implement a Camera Capture flow (preferring the device back camera when available) that lets users take a food photo and then create a log entry from it via an interactive estimation step.

Provide an in-app “AI-like” chat helper experience for diet/nutrition confusion using an on-device/in-app rules + curated FAQ knowledge base (no external LLM calls), including suggested questions and citations to the app’s own guidance.

Add at least one clearly defined “unique” differentiator feature that is not just logging/graphs/chat: implement a “Confidence & Portion Adjuster” step when creating an entry (user adjusts portion size and confidence; calories/nutrients update live and the app stores the confidence value).
Design a simple, easy UI with a coherent visual theme applied consistently across pages and components (colors, typography, spacing, and layout). Avoid a blue/purple default palette.
Add generated static image assets (logo + key illustrations) under frontend/public/assets/generated and render them in the UI (e.g., app header/logo and empty states).
Update app branding to use an aesthetic “S” logo everywhere the app currently shows the NutriScan logo/brand mark, including at minimum the App Header and the Login page.
Add a clearly visible “Scan Food” entry point on the main Dashboard page (next to the existing “Add Entry” primary action) that navigates to the camera capture flow.
When the user navigates to the camera capture page (/camera), start the camera automatically (preferring the back camera) without requiring the user to press a “Start Camera” button.

Update the post-login one-time setup UX to collect all required profile fields, including name plus body-goal onboarding details (goal type, current weight, target weight, weekly goal speed), and block access to the app until the setup is completed.
Show the user’s selected body goal on the Dashboard page after onboarding, including goal type and a compact summary of current vs target weight and weekly goal speed.

Implement a fully local (no external calls) rules-based nutrition estimator backed by a preset list of ~40–50 common Indian + global foods, each with nutrition per 100g (calories, protein, carbs, fat; and the existing micronutrients tracked by the app).

Update the camera scan → estimation flow so that after capture, the app auto-populates food label and nutrition per 100g from the local estimator, and the user only needs to optionally enter the food weight; the app calculates final nutrition automatically from weight.

When the estimator cannot confidently map a scan to a known food, provide a “similar food” fallback by presenting a short list of the closest foods from the preset dataset and letting the user pick one, then proceed with that food’s per-100g nutrition.

Ensure the saved food entry written to the backend reflects the calculated final nutrition values (based on per-100g + optional weight, then portion/confidence adjustments), without requiring the user to manually type calories/macros.

Add an optional speech-to-text (voice dictation) input in the food scanning flow so the user can speak a meal description, have it converted into text, and then manually edit it before saving the scanned entry.
Persist the spoken/edited meal description from the scan confirmation step into the saved food entry’s label/description so the spoken summary is stored and visible in existing entry lists/details.

Add an automatic weekly (last 7 days) summary section that generates goal-aligned feedback, including macro/nutrition suggestions and a 1–10 rating with a congratulatory message when the user is on track.
Make the weekly rating visually engaging by rendering a 1–10 score as a clear rating visualization (e.g., stars or a segmented scale) consistent with the existing UI style.
Generate weekly feedback using fully local, deterministic rules (no external calls), leveraging the user’s stored body goal (if available) and the logged macros/calories for the last 7 days.

In the scan confirmation (EstimationConfirmationStep) UI, make the voice dictation button ("Speak" / "Stop") more prominent by styling it with a blue appearance and a medium size while keeping its existing behavior (start/stop dictation) and conditional rendering (only when speech-to-text is supported).
Add an Android WebView wrapper project to the repository that packages the existing NutriScan web app into a buildable Android APK suitable for Google Play Store submission.
Make the WebView wrapper configurable for the target NutriScan web URL (e.g., production canister URL), without requiring code changes for switching environments.

Ensure Internet Identity login works reliably inside the Android wrapper by handling external-window/redirect flows appropriately (e.g., opening authentication in the system browser or Chrome Custom Tabs and returning to the app).

Ensure camera-based scanning and photo capture work inside the Android wrapper by requesting the correct Android permissions and allowing camera access from WebView (including HTTPS requirement and permission prompts).
Add Play Store–oriented documentation to the repository describing how to build a release APK/AAB, configure signing, set the appId/package name, and where to set the production URL.
Update the React web app’s user-facing branding text from "NutriScan" to "Calorieman" wherever it appears in the UI, including the header brand label and the login page title.
Update the browser tab title to use the app name "Calorieman" (and keep the rest of the title text in English).
Update the Android WebView wrapper’s user-facing app name from "NutriScan" to "Calorieman" in Android string resources and any visible documentation headings referencing the old app name.
Update internal Android wrapper theme naming to match the new app name, ensuring the app continues to build and run with no visual regressions from the current theme.

Perform a repo-wide pass over user-facing strings to ensure remaining references to "NutriScan" that represent the app name are updated to "Calorieman" (without changing technical identifiers like package names unless explicitly required).

Update the post-login profile setup flow to collect the additional profile fields needed for BMI and maintenance calorie calculation (height, age, sex, activity level) and persist them to the backend as part of the caller’s profile.

Add a persistent “Maintenance Calories” area on the Dashboard that is visible whenever the user is logged in and shows: (1) the user’s maintenance calories (TDEE), (2) today’s consumed calories, (3) whether today is above/below/equal to maintenance (with the numeric difference), and (4) the user’s BMI with a simple category label. If the profile is missing required inputs, show an English prompt telling the user which profile fields are needed.

Rename the app/website user-facing name to “Calorieshivam” across the web app and Android wrapper, updating all visible branding strings (header brand label, login page title, image alt text, footer copyright, browser tab title) and Android wrapper user-facing name and documentation headings. Keep technical identifiers (e.g., Android package name, variable/resource keys like `nutriscan_base_url`) unchanged unless strictly necessary for build correctness.

Update the Android wrapper documentation to support a non–Play Store distribution flow (sideload), including clear steps to build a release APK/AAB, where to set the production canister URL, and how a user can install the APK on an Android device.

Fix Android wrapper branding consistency so the installed Android app shows the correct, unique user-facing app name and does not contain leftover internal naming (e.g., the current theme name reference). Ensure the Android wrapper builds successfully after the change.

Add a small in-web “Install App” entry point that explains (in English) how to get the Android app build (sideload) and what it is (a packaged version of the web app). This should reduce confusion for users who expect an app instead of a website.

Make the user-facing app display name configurable from a single place for both the web app (header/login/tab title/alt text) and the Android wrapper (app_name string), so the owner can choose a more searchable unique name without hunting through multiple files.

Ensure the existing Android WebView wrapper can produce an installable release APK (sideload) via a single documented Gradle command, without requiring any code changes to switch the target web app URL.

Add a clear, complete, English sideload build section to `frontend/android-wrapper/README.md` that explains how to set the production canister URL, generate a release APK, and where to find the resulting APK file.

Make release signing optional-but-supported for producing a truly install-ready APK: allow configuring a release signing config via Gradle properties (recommended via `local.properties` or environment variables) and document it in the Android wrapper README.

Add a reproducible packaging flow that builds the Android wrapper release APK and copies/exports it to a stable, web-downloadable location inside the web frontend (e.g., a committed path under `frontend/public/` such as `frontend/public/downloads/Calorieshivam.apk`, or an equivalent single, documented output path), without requiring code changes to switch environments (the wrapped web URL must continue to come from `frontend/android-wrapper/gradle.properties` via `nutriscan.baseUrl`).

Update the in-web Install App page to provide a direct APK download link/button when the packaged APK is present in the frontend’s static assets, and update Step 1 copy to reference downloading the APK directly from the website (English user-facing text only).
Ensure the Android wrapper release APK is produced and placed at `frontend/public/downloads/Calorieshivam.apk` so it is served as a static asset by the deployed web app.
Make the in-web Install App page show the APK as available and allow downloading it when `/downloads/Calorieshivam.apk` exists in static assets.

Provide a complete, copy-pasteable sideload build workflow that produces a release APK for the Android WebView wrapper and exports it to the stable static-asset location `frontend/public/downloads/Calorieshivam.apk`.
Add a new authenticated UI area for “Health Records” where users can add and view personal track record entries for labs and vitals, using English user-facing text.
Add navigation entry points so users can easily find and use Health Records from the existing logged-in experience (without disrupting existing dashboard, logging, scanning, chat, or install flows).
Display the caller’s baseline health snapshot (latest hemoglobin/platelets/BP high/BP low when available) in a compact, read-only summary card so the user can see their starting point at a glance.

new_feature_requests.summary: Daily calorie tracking with end-of-day/period total calorie summary
Camera (back camera) food scanning to estimate approximate calories and basic nutrition (macro/micronutrients)
Graphs and rating/engagement visualizations for calorie/nutrition progress
In-app AI chat assistant to answer user questions and resolve diet/nutrition confusion
Simple, easy-to-use, interactive UI with differentiation/unique features vs typical diet apps
Add a simple daily logging data model and persistence for food entries including: timestamp (day), food label/name, estimated calories, and basic nutrients (macros + a small set of micronutrients).
Update branding: use an aesthetic “S” logo (for Shivam) everywhere in the app (replacing current logo in header/splash/empty states).
Make food scanning discoverable: add a Scan button on the main dashboard that opens the camera immediately.
Local rules-based food recognition + nutrition estimation from scanned images using a built-in Indian+global food list, with a 'similar food' fallback when unknown.
Scan flow update: after prediction, show nutrition per-100g and allow optional user-entered food weight to compute final calories/macros automatically (minimize manual entry).
One-time post-login body-goal onboarding: select goal type (lose/gain/muscle/maintain) and collect current weight, target weight, and weekly goal speed; persist and show on dashboard.

Extend the user profile data model to persist one-time body-goal onboarding details: goal type (Lose Weight, Gain Weight, Gain Muscle, Maintain Weight & Muscle), current weight, target weight, and weekly goal speed.
Add optional speech-to-text voice input in the food scanning flow so users can speak a meal description, convert to text, then manually edit before saving.
Add an automatic weekly (7-day) summary with goal-aligned feedback: macro/nutrition suggestions and a 1–10 score/rating with congratulatory messaging when on track.
Make the voice input button in the scan summary step more prominent (blue color, medium size).
Package the existing NutriScan web app as an Android APK (WebView wrapper) suitable for uploading to the Google Play Store.
Add BMI calculation (and related health metrics as needed) using user profile data (e.g., height/weight) and surface it in the app.
Collect additional user profile fields needed to compute maintenance calories (TDEE)—e.g., height, age, sex, activity level—stored per logged-in user.

Compute and display each user’s maintenance calories (TDEE) locally from profile data, and show a persistent Dashboard section indicating whether today’s calories are above/below/equal to maintenance.
Rename app/website user-facing name to "calorieshivam" (update branding text such as header/login title/tab title and Android app name accordingly).

Extend the per-user profile data model to store the additional fields required to compute BMI and maintenance calories (TDEE), including at minimum: height, age, sex, and activity level, while preserving existing fields (name, bodyGoal) and keeping data isolated per Internet Identity principal.

Add backend logic to compute BMI and maintenance calories (TDEE) deterministically from the caller’s stored profile data, and expose it via a dedicated query API that the frontend can call (e.g., `getCallerHealthMetrics`). Include computed values at minimum: BMI, BMI category label, BMR, and TDEE (maintenance calories).

Provide a standalone installable mobile app experience (at minimum an Android APK that can be installed outside the Play Store / sideload), and ensure the app identity/name is unique and discoverable vs the website

Extend `frontend/android-wrapper/README.md` with a complete, copy-pasteable section explaining how to (1) set `nutriscan.baseUrl`, (2) run the single packaging command/script, and (3) locate the resulting APK file that is meant to be shared for direct download (English documentation only).
Make the Android APK available for direct download (host in a stable web-accessible location and expose a clear download link/button in the web UI).

Complete `frontend/android-wrapper/README.md` so the “Sideload Distribution (Outside Play Store)” section is fully written in English and includes: (1) exactly where/how to set `nutriscan.baseUrl` in `frontend/android-wrapper/gradle.properties`, (2) a single command to run the packaging script, and (3) where to find the resulting APK file.

Add a personal health track record feature so users can enter and store baseline lab/vitals values (e.g., CBC results like hemoglobin and platelet levels, and blood pressure high/low) to form a starting health profile for future reference.

Add backend support for per-user personal health track records so a signed-in user can store and retrieve lab/vitals measurements (including CBC metrics like hemoglobin and platelets, and blood pressure values) as part of their health profile baseline.
Add backend support for a “baseline snapshot” derived from the user’s track records that can be used as a starting point (e.g., latest value per metric), and expose it via a dedicated query API.
